title: Fresh chicken, cream on bread, and working his way through school
summary: He recalls eating farm-fresh food, unable later to eat store-bought chicken in New York, and cleaning the academic building to pay tuition.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: As I say, I had a good life. Because by having that farm life... I remember if we wanted to have some chicken, we just took one of those old... I guess we had them coat-hangers then. We'd stretch them out and bend that wire at the end, go out there and catch a chicken, wring his neck off, heat the water, take his feathers off... And for a long time, when I'd come to New York, I could not eat store-

bought chicken, because I'd been used to eating fresh chicken -- we'd kill it and we'd eat it that day! And I found out where the stores were you could go and have the chickens killed first, and that's the only way I could eat it. Because I couldn't eat no store-bought chicken, because it didn't taste right!

And for breakfast... Man, if we wanted to have some eggs, my mother would say, "Go out in the hen-house and see if there's any eggs." We'd go out there, and they'd laid three or four eggs, or four or five eggs. And we had this cow... I remember, I used to put... We had an icebox and put ice in it; they didn't have refrigerators then...

And I'd go to the icebox and take this bowl of milk, and we'd put the bowl of milk in there, and it would settle overnight, and the cream would come to the top. I'd go get me a piece of bread, and put the piece of bread on top of the cream, and the cream would stick to the bread, and I'd turn it over and put some sugar on it -- and man, that was a thing!
I found out later on that my sister did it. Maybe I learned it from her. And my mother, she saw to it that I got off to school. But see, after I got to school, I

I cleaned the academic building, so I made enough money for my tuition. Because that's another thing in school; they had ways you could work your way through. And when I got there, that's the only way I could have a job. Wasn't nothin' but cleaning. Because I learned how to clean when I was a kid...
